Meta Test Description: The testcase performs PCIe device enumeration across two dual-mode controllers (DM0 and DM1). It begins by writing 0x0 to 0xE6004100 to initialize the system. It then invokes link training (link_training_dm0_x4 or link_training_dm1_x4) based on compile-time defines (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, DM1_EP). Cache coherency programming is performed by reading mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF and mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF, modifying specific bit fields using set_data at bit positions [11:14], [3:6], [27:30], and [19:22] with value 0xf, and writing back. A wait_on(20) delay is inserted between coherency programming phases. The test then polls read_sii0_reg(0xC0) in a while loop until (data_rd & 0xD1) == 0xD1, and similarly polls read_sii1_reg(0xC0) for the same link-up condition. Under DM0_RC, the Vendor ID is read from read_pcie_slv0_reg(0x0), the command register is written via write_pcie_slv0_reg(0x4, 0x7) to enable IO, Memory, and Bus Master, and memory base programming functions mem_base_program_dm0_x4 and mem_base_program_dm1_x4 are called. System-level registers at 0xE690000C, 0xE6900010, 0xE6900014, 0xE6900018, 0xE6900030, and 0xE6900034 are written with 0x1. Cache coherency is then disabled by writing 0x0 to bit fields [19:22] and [27:30] of both COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF registers. After a wait_on(30), BAR sizing is performed on the endpoint via write_pcie_slv1_reg and read_pcie_slv1_reg for offsets 0x10, 0x14, 0x18, 0x1c, 0x20, 0x24 by writing 0xFFFFFFFF, reading back, then writing actual base addresses. The same BAR sizing sequence is repeated for slv0. Finally, the test polls 0xE6004100 in a while loop until the value equals 0x12345678, then calls finish(0).

Meta Test Description: The testcase performs PCIe DMA write and read operations across four channels on either DM0 or DM1 controller. It begins by writing 0x0 to 0xE6004100 to initialize the system. Link training is invoked via link_training_dm0_x4(4) or link_training_dm1_x4(4) based on compile-time defines (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, DM1_EP). Under DM0_RC, the test polls read_sii0_reg(0xC0) in a while loop until (data_rd & 0xD1) == 0xD1 to confirm link-up. The Vendor ID is read via read_pcie_slv0_reg(0x0) and printed. The command register is written via write_pcie_slv0_reg(0x4, 0x7) to enable IO, Memory, and Bus Master. BAR programming is performed via bar_program_dm0_x4(), followed by wait_on(10) and mem_base_program_dm0_x4(). Under DM1_RC, equivalent operations are performed using sii1, slv1, and dm1 variants. The test then calls non_secure_prot_nic() and polls 0xE6004100 in a while loop until the value equals 0x12345678 with wait_on(5) between iterations. Source memory at src_addr0 (0xE6000000) is preloaded with 128 words of 0xC0DEBEED and 128 words of 0xF00DDEAF at offset +400. DMA transfer length is set to 0x40. Write destination addresses are set to 0xA7000000-0xA7004000 for DM0_RC or 0xC7000000-0xC7004000 for DM1_RC. Read destination addresses are set to 0xE6001000 and 0xE6020000. GIC_Set() and GIC_EnableAllIRQ() are called to enable interrupt handling. Under DM0_RC, DMA write interrupt mask is cleared by writing 0x0 to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF and DMA read interrupt mask is cleared by writing 0x0 to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF. For each of the four DMA write channels (0-3), the channel is programmed via program_dma_wch0/1/2/3() with source address, write address, and length parameters, then the doorbell is rung by writing the channel number to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF. After each doorbell write, the test waits in a while(int_pend) loop with wait_on(10) until the interrupt handler clears int_pend, then resets int_pend to 1 and calls wait_on(10). The same sequence is repeated for four DMA read channels (0-3) using program_dma_rch0/1/2/3() and mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF. Under DM1_RC, equivalent operations use mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF, mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF, mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF, mizar_PCIE1_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF, and program_dma1_wch/rch variants. The Default_IRQHandler() reads mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF (or PCIE1 variants for DM1_RC), masks with 0x0000000F to extract channel status, clears interrupts by writing the status to mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and mizar_PCIE0_DBI_DSP_DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF (or PCIE1 variants), sets int_pend to 0, and calls GIC_ClearIRQ(0x20) for DM0 or GIC_ClearIRQ(0x23) for DM1. The test concludes with wait_on(10) and finish(0).

Three SII register addresses are stored in sii0_addr[]: mizar_PCIE0_SII_PCIE0_TRANSMIT_HEADER2, mizar_PCIE0_SII_PCIE0_TRANSMIT_HEADER3, mizar_PCIE0_SII_PHY_CONTROL_23, with corresponding sii1_addr[] for PCIE1.
